distractors.reason: We don't say 'believe on'. 'On' follows verbs like depend on, rely on, count on.
We don't say 'believe at'. 'At' follows verbs like look at, smile at, laugh at.
We don't say 'believe for'. 'For' follows verbs like wait for, ask for, look for.

example_sentence: She always believed ___ her dream of becoming a doctor.
l1_interference: Українське дієслово «вірити» може керувати давальним відмінком без прийменника («вірити мрії»), тому носії часто кажуть «believe the dream» замість «believe in the dream». В англійській мові для цього значення обов'язково потрібен прийменник «in».
explanation: 'Believe in' is used when we trust a person, a principle or an idea, or have faith in them. Compare 'I believe you' (I think what you say is true) with 'I believe in you' (I have faith in you).

related_collocations.example: Her success depends on hard work.
He listened to his grandmother's stories every night.
Look at this old photo of my grandfather.

memory_tip: BELIEVE IN = trust a person, an idea or a dream | BELIEVE + clause = think something is true (I believe it is true)
